newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices retreat ahead of weekend.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices retreat ahead of weekend.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices eased ahead of the weekend Friday as temperatures moderated across most of the Midwest and cooler weather was forecast for the West late this weekend, market sources said.
Prices at the Henry Hub, La, on average lost six cents to $2.17-2.20 per mmBtu, while Transco (Station 65) was quoted mostly in the low-$2.20s.
The work on Transco's Texas line will continue to cut the line's total capacity of about 600 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) through Monday, with 400 mmcfd still cut May 20-22.
South Texas prices slipped by an equal amount to $2.05-2.10 despite forecasts calling for slightly warmer weather this weekend.
In the East, where temperatures are still normal to slightly below normal, New York city-gate prices fell by more than five cents to the low-to-mid $2.40s.
Appalachian prices similarly slid to about $2.37-2.39 on Columbia and CNG.
In the Midcontinent, where milder temperatures are expected to arrive Sunday and Monday, prices slipped eight cents to the high-$1.90s.
A cold front is expected to usher in more below-normal temperatures on Tuesday, Weather Services Corp said.
In west Texas, Permian prices tumbled 11 cents to a wide range of $1.91-1.98 as cooler air was forecast to arrive in the Southwest Sunday.
As a result of the foreast, Southern California border prices were also down at $2.13-2.14.
